agent_explanations_oldest_first.text:
Reversing the columns gives a clear dose-response. P("However") at the doubt decisions falls from 0.79 (original) to 0.54 (zeroed) to 0.24 (reversed). It is now top-1 in only 20 of 74 cases, replaced by ordinary continuations ("The", "Since", "We").

The cost is small. The true token at control decisions loses 0.003 nats, and mean answer-token log-probability falls by 0.011 on cut texts and 0.003 on controls. So the eight neurons do drive the doubt-and-restart token, and reversing them mostly removes the reflex.

Now the real test is accuracy, in generation. I'll run a paired "both" pass with E3 alone, without n3729, so the doubt mechanism is measured on its own. To avoid testing on the problems whose answers selected the neurons, the set is DEV[1024:1200] (176 untouched problems), plus 80 DEV problems that were in none of the pass-10 texts.

How to read the result:
- **Confirmed:** fewer cuts and a positive paired accuracy difference of about +2 points or more.
- **Refuted:** fewer cuts but flat accuracy. That would mean the doubt was a symptom of being stuck, not a cause of failure.

The test set dev_d has 256 distinct problems, and E3 (the eight doubt-neuron columns reversed) is saved. I'm running the paired generation now. The prediction is fewer cut-offs and a positive paired accuracy difference.

Removing the token did not remove the loop. "However" fell from 7% to 2.3% of answers, and from 68% to 18% of cut answers, but cuts did not drop. In the edited model, loops restart with other line openers instead, mostly "The".

So "However" was the most common surface form of a restart, not its cause. Of the 12 wrong-to-right flips, 9 came from wrong finished answers and only 3 from cut ones. The +2.0 ± 1.7 is therefore not a loop fix, and part of it may be noise or a mild side effect.

E3 is still the best measured candidate, so I'll save a copy to /work/best_1.

Next I'll test whether E3 and the n3729 regime ablation add up. n3729 alone gave +1.2 ± 1.9 by moving problems into the stronger R1 mode, and E3 does not touch that neuron. I'll run "both" on 256 fresh DEV problems: none was used in the pass-10 texts or in dev_d, all from DEV[:1024].

A combined gain of about +3 or more would make the combination the main candidate. A gain no larger than E3's would mean the two do not stack, and I'd keep the simpler edit.
